title: Make mypy pass after elevations became optional (`or 0.0` is the trap)
prompt: `mypy` (strict mode, configured in `pyproject.toml`) reports errors in `src/`. Fix them so that `mypy` passes, without `# type: ignore`, `cast`, `Any`, or changes to the mypy configuration.

setup.new: ele: float | None  # metres; None where the GPS lost it

setup.old: points = [Point(point.lat, point.lon, point.ele * scale) for point in points]
lat, lon, ele = (float(part) for part in fields)
setup.new:
lat, lon = float(fields[0]), float(fields[1])
        ele = float(fields[2]) if fields[2] else None

setup.old:
- Each point has three numbers. Latitude must be within -90 to 90 and longitude within
  -180 to 180, both inclusive.
setup.new:
- Each point has three numbers. Latitude must be within -90 to 90 and longitude within
  -180 to 180, both inclusive.
- The elevation may be left empty (`42.2031,23.3205,`) where the GPS lost it. Such a
  point keeps `ele=None` and still counts for distance. Everywhere else (ascent and
  descent, highest and lowest, steepest grade and walking time) it takes the elevation
  of the nearest earlier point that has one or, if there is none, of the nearest later
  point.

edits.old: gain_and_loss([point.ele for point in track.points], threshold)

edits.new: elevations = [point.ele or 0.0 for point in track.points]
counted_changes([p.ele or 0.0 for p in track.points])

edits.old: gain_and_loss([point.ele for point in track.points], threshold)
edits.new: gain_and_loss([point.ele or 0.0 for point in track.points], threshold)
